MARKETS — MORNING EDITION, SUNDAY 25 OCTOBER 2026. Read 08:03 GMT.

*** THE FIRST EDITION ON GREENWICH MEAN TIME. The clocks went back at 02:00 this morning. ***
Verified at publication: tm_isdst = 0, zone = GMT, UTC offset 0. The tool that stamps the ticker
timestamp now derives the offset from the edition's own date and time rather than a hardcoded value,
and was tested this morning against six cases either side of the change before being used.

*** THE HONEST POSITION, STATED FOR THE THIRD EDITION RUNNING ***
Nine of our ten markets have been shut since Friday afternoon. These nine figures are the SAME
Friday closes published in our Saturday morning and Saturday evening editions. A reader comparing
the three will see an unchanged ticker, and that is correct rather than stale. Bitcoin is the only
market that trades through the weekend and the only figure that has moved. Markets reopen tomorrow.

Bitcoin               80,532.28    +0.15   *** LIVE — the only open market. SIGN DISPUTED, see below ***
10y UST                   5.00     +0.05   Friday's close

THE ONE MOVE — AND THE TWO PROVIDERS DISAGREE ON ITS DIRECTION
  Level:   CNBC 80,532.28   vs  Trading Economics 80,520   -> AGREE to within about $12.
  Change:  CNBC +0.15%      vs  Trading Economics -0.34%   -> *** THE SIGNS DISAGREE. ***
  Both are internally defensible: a continuously traded instrument has no fixed daily close, so each
  provider measures a rolling 24-hour window from its own reference point. CNBC's figure is coherent
  against its own stated previous close (80,532.28 - 118.13 = 80,414.15), and its previous-close
  field has itself moved from 81,207 yesterday to 80,414 today for exactly that reason.
  *** CONSEQUENCE FOR THE COPY: no directional claim about Bitcoin appears in this edition. ***
  It would have been easy and wrong to write that it "turned positive overnight" — it was down more
  than 1% when we published at 19:55 last night, and CNBC now shows a small gain — but a cross-check
  that disagrees on sign cannot support a claim about direction. The LEVEL is published, the feed's
  change is carried in the ticker where it belongs, and the prose says only that it is the one market
  trading. This is the same discipline applied to the gilt on 20 October, when one feed's drifted
  previous close inverted a fall into a rise.

CROSS-CHECK
  Bitcoin is the only figure that can have changed and the only one re-checked.
  The nine closed markets were cross-checked on Saturday morning at 11:21 and those checks stand:
  the FTSE agreed to the penny across both providers, the gilt agreed on level, and the ten-year
  Treasury agreed on level and change at 5.00%.

DECLARATIONS CARRIED FORWARD, STILL TRUE
  1. Trading Economics' Brent page was $13.45 low on Saturday — the eleventh consecutive day wrong by
     roughly $8 to $14. The oil level rests on the primary feed alone.
  2. The ten-year Treasury reads 4.999% on one feed and 5.00% on the other. NO CLAIM THAT IT HAS
     FALLEN BELOW 5% APPEARS ANYWHERE, for the fourth consecutive edition.
  3. The feed's previous-close field for the gilt has drifted repeatedly, so the published day-move
     rests on our own Friday-afternoon reading.

NOTE ON THIS EDITION: a scheduled run was live and healthy when this edition was begun — 64 cache
files in its first five minutes, and its internal day-count checked out as correct. It was stopped
because the editor had asked for the brief to be produced by hand, because its prompt still mandates
a block that is vetoed on this site, and because two processes writing index.html at once is a real
risk. Its research was harvested in full and is relied upon below. This is the eighth consecutive
scheduled slot not published by the automation, but the first in which the automation was working.
